vendors.name: IBM watsonx.data
vendors.tagline: IBM open lakehouse. A separate governance product adds glossary, text-to-SQL, and MCP.
vendors.verdictNote: The lakehouse has no semantic model, but watsonx.data intelligence adds a glossary, enrichment, text-to-SQL, and an MCP server, and watsonx BI adds a metrics catalog.

artifacts.name: watsonx.data intelligence MCP server (managed)
artifacts.format: Remote MCP endpoint with API key; IBM calls it tech preview; Software edition planned for June 2026

artifacts.name: Data Intelligence MCP server (open source)
artifacts.format: Python package on PyPI; stdio or HTTP; SaaS or Cloud Pak for Data 5.2.1 and later

artifacts.name: watsonx.data MCP server (managed, SaaS)
artifacts.format: Remote MCP for engines, catalogs, SQL and Spark; IBM gives no stage label

artifacts.name: Text2SQL in watsonx.data intelligence
artifacts.format: UI and MCP tools; container must be enabled for text-to-SQL; no stage label found

artifacts.name: Metadata enrichment and business glossary
artifacts.format: UI, MCP tools, CSV import; AI-generated names, descriptions and term assignments

artifacts.name: watsonx BI metrics catalog
artifacts.format: UI; metrics and business concepts; separate product from watsonx.data

artifacts.name: Milvus vector database in watsonx.data
artifacts.format: Managed Milvus service in the console

metrics.n: The metrics catalog is in watsonx BI, a separate product. watsonx.data itself holds no metric objects.

dimensions.n: watsonx BI models business concepts and metrics. The lakehouse has no dimension or hierarchy objects.

relationships.n: Metadata enrichment runs primary key and foreign key analysis. The semantic model tool returns foreign keys to the text-to-SQL agent.

synonyms.n: Glossary terms and AI-generated descriptions attach to assets. The MCP server returns them to agents.

verifiedQueries.n: No store of approved question and SQL pairs appears in the install guide or MCP tool list. Text-to-SQL context comes from enriched metadata.

nl2sql.n: Text2SQL launched in 2025. Docs and sources show no stage label, so the level stays at 2.

ontology.n: Glossary terms, classifications, data classes, and data products. No object, link, or action model was found.

graph.n: No graph query language appears in the watsonx.data intelligence docs. Lineage graphs exist in the catalog.

vector.n: Managed Milvus ships in watsonx.data. Enrichment also vectorizes metadata for text-to-SQL.

mcp.n: An open-source server on PyPI covers glossary, lineage, enrichment and text-to-SQL. A managed endpoint is in tech preview.

governance.n: MCP calls use the caller's permissions. IBM says masking and protection rules apply at query time.

openStandard.n: IBM does not appear in the Apache Ossie working group lists. No semantic model export appears in the docs.

aiDescriptions.n: Gen AI enrichment drafts table names, column names, descriptions, glossary terms, and term assignments.

bulkMetadata.n: MCP tools import glossary CSV files and run enrichment jobs. Enrichment also runs from the UI.

autoClassify.n: Enrichment assigns data classes and classifications. An MCP tool applies sensitivity labels to assets.

sampleValues.n: The semantic model tool returns profiling data and sample values when they exist. It depends on the text-to-SQL feature.

queryHistory.n: The Text-to-SQL and MCP tool docs show no mining of query history. Context comes from enrichment and vectors.

lineage.n: The catalog gives upstream and downstream lineage graphs through MCP. Column-level depth is not confirmed in the sources.

evals.n: IBM certifies models for Text-to-SQL, but no customer test set or rating loop appears in the docs.

vendors.enrichHowTo: Run a metadata enrichment job in watsonx.data intelligence on the target tables. It drafts names, descriptions, and glossary term assignments with an LLM. Then import business terms in bulk with the glossary CSV import tool and enable the project for text-to-SQL.
offers: Glossary, classifications, and data classes in watsonx.data intelligence give an agent business meaning for columns.
Gen AI enrichment drafts names, descriptions, and term assignments, and vectorizes metadata for text-to-SQL.
An open-source MCP server exposes search, lineage, quality, glossary, and text-to-SQL tools to any MCP client.
Text-to-SQL tools read a semantic model with keys, foreign keys, profiling data, and sample values.
Milvus runs as a service in watsonx.data for vector search.
gaps: The lakehouse has no declared metric or dimension objects. Metrics sit in watsonx BI, a separate product.
The managed MCP endpoint is in tech preview. Some text-to-SQL tools do not work in the AWS US East region.
No verified question and SQL pair feature was found in the sources read.
Key IBM docs pages return 403 to scripts, so stage labels are hard to confirm.
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Enrich the tables in watsonx.data intelligence and assign glossary terms. Enable the project for text-to-SQL. Then connect your agent through the open-source MCP server so it reads the semantic model before it writes SQL.

vendors.name: Cloudera
vendors.tagline: Hybrid data platform with Impala, Hive, Iceberg, a catalog, and a Hue SQL assistant.
vendors.verdictNote: No semantic layer or metric model was found. The SQL AI Assistant reads table metadata and three sample rows, and an Iceberg MCP server gives raw SQL access.

artifacts.name: SQL AI Assistant in Cloudera Data Explorer (Hue)
artifacts.format: UI; admin picks an LLM host; launched as tech preview, current docs show no stage label

artifacts.name: AI visual in Cloudera Data Visualization
artifacts.format: UI; admin enables it under AI Settings; version 7 docs said technical preview, version 8 docs show no label

artifacts.name: Cloudera Iceberg MCP server (via Impala)
artifacts.format: Open-source Python server; tools execute_query and get_schema; read-only

artifacts.name: Cloudera Semantic Search
artifacts.format: Vector database service on OpenSearch; docs call it a technical preview

artifacts.name: Atlas glossary, tags and business metadata
artifacts.format: UI, CSV import, Atlas REST API

artifacts.name: Cloudera Data Lineage (formerly Octopai)
artifacts.format: Lineage platform with connectors; acquired from Octopai

metrics.n: No governed metric objects found. Teams define metrics in BI tools or SQL views.

dimensions.n: No dimension or hierarchy objects found in the lakehouse docs.

relationships.n: The SQL AI Assistant sends keys and constraints from the schema. Atlas holds no declared join model for AI.

synonyms.n: Atlas glossary terms and business metadata exist. No doc says the SQL AI Assistant reads them.

verifiedQueries.n: No verified query feature found in the SQL AI Assistant or Data Visualization docs.

nl2sql.n: SQL AI Assistant launched as tech preview in 2024. Current docs show no stage label, so the level stays at 2.

ontology.n: Atlas glossary and classifications only. No object, link, or action model was found.

graph.n: Atlas keeps metadata in JanusGraph and shows lineage graphs. The docs show no graph query language for users.

vector.n: Cloudera Semantic Search offers vector and lexical search on OpenSearch. Docs call it a technical preview.

mcp.n: The Iceberg MCP server for Impala is in preview. It gives execute_query and get_schema, read-only.

governance.n: Cloudera says its MCP servers keep SDX policies. The assistant shares only data the signed-in user can see.

openStandard.n: Cloudera joined the Apache Ossie working group in 2026. The docs show no Ossie import or export in a product.

aiDescriptions.n: The SQL AI Assistant summarizes queries but does not write table or column descriptions. Data Catalog descriptions are manual.

bulkMetadata.n: Atlas imports glossary terms and business metadata in bulk from CSV or XLS. The Atlas REST API also writes tags.

autoClassify.n: Data Catalog profilers apply Atlas tags automatically. The Data Compliance and Cluster Sensitivity profilers do this.

sampleValues.n: The SQL AI Assistant sends three sample rows per table to the LLM. It does not match literals to values.

queryHistory.n: Hue shows query history to users. The docs do not say the SQL AI Assistant mines it for context.

lineage.n: Cloudera Data Lineage (Octopai) adds lineage for Spark, Hive, Impala, Databricks, and Snowflake. Column-level depth is not confirmed.

evals.n: The docs list model limits such as hallucination. No feedback loop or test set tool appears.

vendors.enrichHowTo: Write descriptions into the table with SQL comments in Hive or Impala, then import glossary terms and business metadata through the Atlas CSV import. Apply tags in bulk with the Atlas bulk classification REST endpoint. The SQL AI Assistant does not document a way to read glossary terms.
offers: The SQL AI Assistant in Hue writes, edits, fixes, and explains Hive and Impala SQL from a prompt.
The assistant uses RAG. It sends table names, column types, keys, partitions, constraints, and three sample rows to the LLM.
An open-source Iceberg MCP server lets agents list tables and run read-only SQL on Impala.
Atlas gives tags, glossary, and business metadata. Octopai-based Cloudera Data Lineage gives cross-system lineage.
Cloudera Semantic Search gives vector and keyword search for RAG, in technical preview.
gaps: No semantic model, metric definitions, or declared join paths exist for AI to read.
The assistant cannot exclude chosen tables from its context, according to the 2024 launch blog.
The MCP server and Semantic Search are in preview. The MCP server gives only two tools.
No evals, verified queries, or query history mining were found in the docs.
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Use the Iceberg MCP server so an agent reads the schema and runs read-only SQL on Impala. Put a semantic layer such as Cube or dbt on top, because Cloudera has none. Keep descriptions in table comments and the Atlas glossary.

vendors.name: StarTree
vendors.tagline: Managed Apache Pinot for real-time analytics, with an AI agent and Spaces.
vendors.verdictNote: CosmiQ Spaces hold descriptions, rules, joins, and verified queries for Pinot tables, but Spaces are a proprietary text context and not a typed metric model.

artifacts.name: CosmiQ Spaces
artifacts.format: UI editor and REST API; descriptions, synonyms, rules, joins, query policy, verified queries; docs show no stage label

artifacts.name: CosmiQ conversational analytics agent
artifacts.format: Chat UI, REST API, and a text_to_sql MCP tool; runs Claude on AWS Bedrock

artifacts.name: StarTree MCP Server for Apache Pinot
artifacts.format: Hosted at mcp.<domain>/mcp with OAuth; open-source base mcp-pinot; install through StarTree

artifacts.name: Vector index
artifacts.format: Table index config; approximate nearest neighbor search

metrics.n: A Space holds canonical metric definitions as plain-text business rules. They are not typed metric objects.

dimensions.n: Spaces store column descriptions, sample values, and time formats. No hierarchy or time grain objects were found.

relationships.n: A Space lists explicit join paths between tables so the agent does not guess.

synonyms.n: Bootstrap and the editor store column descriptions and synonyms. The agent reads them in its prompt.

verifiedQueries.n: Spaces keep question and SQL pairs. Matching uses token overlap and embedding similarity.

nl2sql.n: CosmiQ writes and runs Pinot SQL from plain English. The docs show no stage label.

ontology.n: No entity, link, or action model in the CosmiQ or MCP docs. Teams use Spaces.

graph.n: Pinot queries use SQL. The StarTree Cloud docs index lists no graph query feature.

vector.n: Pinot vector index supports similarity search in StarTree Cloud. Auto embedding is announced, not shipped.

mcp.n: The hosted MCP server lists tables, reads table details, and runs SELECT queries. StarTree installs it for you.

governance.n: Space policy sets read-only mode, row limits, timeouts, and do_not_use columns. Docs do not say Spaces inherit row security.

openStandard.n: Spaces are a StarTree format with no export spec found. The MCP server follows the open MCP protocol.

aiDescriptions.n: Bootstrap samples live data and drafts column descriptions, synonyms, rules, and starter verified queries with an LLM.

bulkMetadata.n: The PATCH Spaces endpoint edits tables, rules, joins, policy, and verified queries through the API.

autoClassify.n: An author can flag columns as do_not_use by hand. The docs show no automatic PII or sensitivity tagging.

sampleValues.n: Bootstrap reads distinct counts, ranges, and sample values for low-cardinality columns and stores them in the Space.

queryHistory.n: The Query Analyzer mines slow queries for tuning advice. No doc says it builds semantic context.

lineage.n: The StarTree Cloud docs index lists no lineage page. Teams use an external catalog for lineage.

evals.n: Thumbs up and down ratings feed a suggestions endpoint that proposes verified queries. No benchmark tool was found.

vendors.enrichHowTo: Call POST /api/bootstrap/space on the Pinot tables. It drafts descriptions, synonyms, joins, rules, and starter verified queries. Review the draft, then edit it with PATCH /api/spaces/{id}.
offers: Spaces give the agent column descriptions, synonyms, business rules, join paths, and verified queries for each Pinot table.
Bootstrap drafts a Space from table schema, config, and sampled live data, so teams review instead of write.
Query policy sets read-only mode, row limits, timeouts, and columns the agent must not select.
CosmiQ exposes a text_to_sql MCP tool, and the StarTree MCP server exposes read-only Pinot tools.
Pinot has a vector index for similarity search next to real-time analytics.
gaps: Spaces are free text rules, not typed metrics or dimensions, and no export format was found.
CosmiQ docs show no stage label and no launch date. It runs on Claude through AWS Bedrock.
The StarTree MCP server is installed through StarTree, and the custom context and guardrails features were listed as coming soon.
No lineage, classification, or catalog feature was found in the docs.
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Bootstrap a Space for the Pinot tables and review the draft rules and joins. Add verified queries for the questions people ask most. Then call CosmiQ through its text_to_sql MCP tool or the REST API.

notes.text: The lakehouse is watsonx.data. Governance, glossary, text-to-SQL, and the MCP server are in watsonx.data intelligence. Metrics are in watsonx BI. The page treats them as one vendor.
IBM has two managed MCP servers. One is for watsonx.data intelligence metadata, in tech preview. One is for watsonx.data engines and queries, in SaaS 2.3.2.
Octopai became Cloudera Data Lineage. Cloudera announced the acquisition in November 2024. Hue is now called Cloudera Data Explorer in recent docs.
CosmiQ is a Claude-based agent with a Space as its semantic layer. The docs give no stage label or launch date.
